summary.headline: IRCON FY26 revenue fell to Rs 9,502 crore (from Rs 11,131 crore) and PAT to Rs 592 crore; FY27 revenue guided flat at ~Rs 9,000 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 total revenue was Rs 9,502 crore against Rs 11,131 crore in FY25, and PAT declined to Rs 592 crore from Rs 724 crore. Management said the order book rose to about Rs 24,984 crore (about 2x annual revenue), but sectoral headwinds and tougher bidding competition are pressuring margins. Management said FY26 revenue was about Rs 9,000 crore against earlier guidance of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, citing execution delays beyond its control, and guided FY27 at similar levels. Standalone core EBITDA margin is guided to 4.0-4.2% on the Q&A call (4.0-4.5% in a later answer), with consolidated PAT margin of 6.1-6.3%.

segments.name: Standalone EPC / railways
segments.commentary: Core EBITDA margin guided to 4.0-4.2% (later 4.0-4.5%) as bids are priced aggressively and some go below estimate. Current order book quoted at about Rs 25,000 crore with 2.5-3 year execution.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.commentary: Consolidated core EBITDA margin around 9%, supported by PPP SPVs, and consolidated PAT margin guided at 6.1-6.3%. Consolidated debt of about Rs 5,700 crore is project-level PPP debt at 70:30 to 80:20 D/E, to be repaid over concession periods.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Operating projects in Algeria, Myanmar, Nepal (two projects, land pending) and Sri Lanka and Malaysia; Bangladesh project completed. International profit was boosted by project closure, FX gains and Algeria margin improvement.

segments.name: JVs
segments.commentary: Share of JV profit guided at about Rs 70-80 crore for FY27, excluding Ircon Soma Tollway whose concession ends in FY26-27. CERL losses are expected to narrow and reach break-even in about two years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at about Rs 9,000 crore, similar to FY26, based on the existing order book.
Standalone core EBITDA margin guided at 4.0-4.2% (4.0-4.5% in a later answer); consolidated core EBITDA margin about 9%.

FY27 investment of Rs 700-800 crore in SPV equity and quasi-equity (Rs 400-500 crore for PPP projects per one answer, Rs 500-600 crore in the current year per another), plus Rs 50-60 crore of standalone capex.
Management expects a turnover contribution of 5-7% of a new order's value in the year it is secured.
capex_capacity: Around Rs 400 crore to be invested in SPV projects in FY27, mainly roads and coal connectivity rail.
Total FY27 investment in equity and quasi-equity of Rs 700-800 crore, with Rs 3,000 crore already invested in subsidiaries and JVs.
Standalone routine capex and machinery purchases of Rs 50-60 crore planned for FY27.
No manufacturing businesses currently, apart from one Kavach tower installation project on Central Railway.
demand_pricing: Railway budget FY26 cited at about Rs 2.93 lakh crore sanctioned. Management said FY26 railway orders secured were about Rs 5,000 crore from 107 bids worth about Rs 48,000 crore, most still under evaluation.
Dedicated Freight Corridor (Dhankuni-Surat) just announced; tender timing unclear. Management declined to confirm the Rs 50,000 crore size that an analyst cited.
Win rate by value: about 5.7% in FY24, 6% in FY25 and 10% in FY26.
Competition intensifying: some bids priced well below estimate, and margins are shrinking industry-wide.
Price variation formulas apply to competitive and nomination contracts. Extraordinary bitumen and fuel cost spikes from the Gulf conflict are not fully covered; NHAI issued bitumen relief.
Nomination-basis order book increases reflect scope and cost escalation on cost-plus projects, not new awards from Indian Railways.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue guidance drop from Rs 10,000-11,000 crore to about Rs 9,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to order book conversion difficulties in a tough market and to delays in land and clearances on existing projects. FY26 revenue was about Rs 9,000 crore, and FY27 is guided similar.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia/Gulf crisis put the Rs 9,000 crore revenue at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most FY27 revenue comes from the existing order book and that the impact is not expected immediately. It said the guidance would be reviewed if the crisis is prolonged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of international orders, given no large wins recently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is bidding in Africa but said the Gulf war and energy-price shock are weighing on sentiment. Current overseas projects are in Algeria, Myanmar, Bangladesh (completed), Nepal and Sri Lanka.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated non-current financial liabilities rise to about Rs 6,300 crore from Rs 4,750 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other financial liabilities rose from Rs 584 crore to Rs 821 crore. It did not clearly explain the total increase on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consolidated debt of about Rs 5,700 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the debt is project financing for 15-16 PPP SPVs (roads and highways, plus some coal connectivity rail), repaid over concession periods and not held at standalone level.

risks_watch: Revenue shortfall against earlier guidance (Rs 10,000-11,000 crore to about Rs 9,000 crore) and execution delays on land and clearances.
Margin compression: standalone core EBITDA margin guided down to about 4.0-4.5% amid aggressive bidding.
Win ratio of 10% in FY26 against 107 railway bids worth about Rs 48,000 crore pending evaluation.
Cost escalation from the Gulf conflict and fuel and bitumen prices, which price variation formulas may not fully cover.
CERL losses and Ircon Soma Tollway exit, which affect JV profit (Rs 70-80 crore guided for FY27).
Lumpy working capital and receivables on cost-plus projects, plus the WCDL.
Media reports of a possible IRCON-RVNL merger; management said it has no official communication.
summary.management_tone: Management was cautious and somewhat defensive on the revenue miss, citing external factors such as land delays and competition. It was confident on the long-term pipeline and government spending. Answers on the cost impact of the Gulf conflict and the consolidated liability increase were vague, with figures deferred.
key_quotes: we did manage to maintain the order book at about 2X of the annual revenue
So, FY27, we plan to kind of maintain the numbers that we have in FY26 on revenue because the order book that we have right now is almost about 2X of the revenue.
There are certain times or certain things which get unusually delayed even in the existing order book.
But at a consolidated level, because we have invested in PPP projects and we are getting decent margins there, that is where we are drawing up or I would say equalizing this negative to some extent

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at about Rs 9,000 crore, similar to FY26 and down from the earlier Rs 10,000-11,000 crore guide, backed by a Rs 24,984 crore order book but with no new capacity; standalone core EBITDA margin cut to 4.0-4.5%.
